title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X is a topological (oriented) surface, and 𝒢 is a discrete group acting on X. G ⊲ 𝒢 is a normal subgroup acting properly on X. Each stabilizer G_x acts faithfully near x and preserves the local orientation, so G_x is finite cyclic and acts by rotations. Then Y = X/G is again a topological surface, with projection f: X → Y.

Ramification data. X^! is a discrete 𝒢-stable subset of X. The 'signature' d_X: X^! → ℕ is a 𝒢-invariant function bounding allowed ramification: a covering is 'subordinate to d_X' if its ramification index over x divides d_X(x). By the remark on the next page, the value 0 means 'puncture / unrestricted'; such points are removed. Set Y^! = X^!/G ⊂ Y. One assumes every point with nontrivial G-stabilizer lies in X^!. Define d_Y(f(x)) = |G_x| · d_X(x). This is well defined because d_X is G-invariant and stabilizers along an orbit are conjugate.

Categories. Rev(X, d_X, 𝒢) is the category of 𝒢-equivariant ramified coverings X' → X subordinate to d_X. Rev(Y, d_Y, ℋ), with ℋ = 𝒢/G, is the analogous category on Y.

Claim (completed on the next page). The functor X' ↦ X'/G lands in Rev(Y, d_Y, ℋ) and is an equivalence. A quasi-inverse is the normalized pullback Y' ↦ normalization of Y' ×_Y X.

The case of interest is d_X ≡ 1 on X^! = {x : G_x ≠ 1}. Then Rev(X, d_X, 𝒢) is just the category of unramified 𝒢-coverings of X. So orbifold coverings of Y with indices |G_x| can be read as 𝒢-equivariant étale coverings of X.

Modern language. This is the descent of coverings along the orbifold/stack quotient: coverings of the orbifold (X, d_X) with 𝒢-action ≃ coverings of [X/𝒢] ≃ coverings of the orbifold (Y, d_Y) with ℋ-action. Equivalently, both categories are sets with an action of the same extension of 𝒢 by π_1^orb(X, d_X), which is also an extension of ℋ by π_1^orb(Y, d_Y). It serves the surrounding Longue Marche discussion: identifying cartographic groups and orbifold fundamental groups of M_{0,3}, M_{1,1} (e.g. the link to GL(2,ℤ) on the previous page) by passing between a surface with group action and its quotient orbifold.
errors: No genuine error. Implicit hypotheses: orientation preservation is needed so Y is a surface and the G_x are cyclic; 'subordinate' must mean the ramification index divides d (with 0 meaning puncture/unrestricted). With these, the equivalence (via normalized fibre product) holds. 'Signature' is Grothendieck's informal term for a ramification-bound function.

ideas.what: Equivalence between 𝒢-equivariant ramified coverings of X with bounded ramification d_X and ℋ = 𝒢/G-equivariant ramified coverings of Y = X/G with bound d_Y = |G_x|·d_X, via X' ↦ X'/G, with quasi-inverse given by normalized pullback
ideas.modern_name: Coverings of orbifolds / quotient stacks; orbifold fundamental group exact sequence 1→π_1^orb(X,d)→π_1^orb(Y,d')→G→1; Abhyankar-type normalized base change
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fox (branched coverings, 1957), Thurston (orbifolds, 1978); algebraic tame version Grothendieck–Murre (1971), SGA1 Exp. XIII
ideas.where_published: Spirit present in SGA1 (Galois categories, tame ramification) and in Esquisse d'un programme / La Longue Marche (cartographic groups, multiplicities of orbifold points); this exact formulation unsure

ideas.what: Signature function d: X^! → ℕ prescribing allowed ramification indices (0 = puncture)
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold structure / cone-point multiplicities; root stacks
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Fuchsian group signatures; Thurston; Cadman for root stacks)

deep.surprise_reason: Standard orbifold covering descent, carefully set up as a technical lemma for the Longue Marche computations; nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Crossed-out symbol before 'les stabilisateurs' looks like '𝓗 ⊂ G' (script H), consistent with later ℋ = 𝒢/G.
In 'Pour X' ∈ Ob Rev(X, d_X, 𝒢)' the subscript is written somewhat like d_1 but should read d_X.
'Rev(X, d_X, 𝒢)' is described as 'catégorie des 𝒢-revêtements ramifiés de X, subordonnés à d_X' (the transcription is correct).
